name: Kitesurf & Wingfoil Spots
hero_subtitle: Flat lagoon water, steady trade winds and camps along the shore — one of the world’s great wind-sport classrooms.

overview.title: Why riders choose Dakhla
overview.p1: Consistent side-onshore winds and waist-deep flat water make the lagoon ideal for learning and for long freestyle or freeride sessions. Schools and camps cluster at well-known kilometre markers along the shore.
overview.p2: PK zones and “speed” stretches offer glass when conditions align. Ocean-side spots add waves for advanced riders who want Atlantic energy.
overview.p3: Book lessons or rental through a recognised school. Respect rescue zones, local rules and other water users.

moods.title: Kitesurfing in Dakhla, Session by Session
moods.subtitle: How the wind and water change throughout the day.

1.title: Early flat-water sessions
1.desc: Catch the early breeze when the water is calmest and the lagoon is wide open for long freeride runs.

2.title: Peak wind & school hours
2.desc: The trade winds build to their strongest. Lessons take place in the shallows while experts push freestyle limits.

3.title: Downwinders & beach chill
3.desc: Wind often eases slightly as the sun dips. Relax at the camp beach bars and watch the final kiters on the water.

food.title: Refueling at the Kite Camps
food.p1: Most kite camps feature open-air restaurants and beach terraces overlooking the water, serving fresh seafood, local Moroccan dishes, and healthy post-session meals.
food.li1: Fresh lagoon oysters and grilled fish caught daily.
food.li2: Traditional tagines and couscous served at the camps.
food.li3: Smoothies, fresh juices, and energy bowls for kiters.
food.li4: Mint tea on beach loungers after a long session on the water.
food.li5: Lively social dinners and barbecues hosted by the camps at night.
food.p2: You'll find everything you need right at the water's edge without having to leave the spot.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Kitesurfers in Dakhla

1.title: Equipment & Rentals
1.desc: Most camps offer modern kite, wingfoil, and board rentals. If bringing your own gear, check airline baggage allowances for boardbags.

2.title: Wind & Wetsuits
2.desc: Winds blow strong all year, peaking in summer. Water can feel crisp, so a 3/2mm shorty or full wetsuit is recommended.

3.title: Safety & Etiquette
3.desc: Respect right-of-way rules in the lagoon, keep clear of beginners' zones, and make sure your camp offers rescue boat cover.

title.question: Is it easy to learn kitesurfing in Dakhla?
title.answer: Yes! The combination of shallow, flat water and consistent side-onshore winds makes Dakhla one of the best places in the world for beginners.

title.question: Do I need to bring my own equipment?
title.answer: Not necessarily. Almost all kite camps offer high-end gear rental, though many experienced kiters prefer bringing their own familiar setup.

title.question: What is the wind season in Dakhla?
title.answer: Dakhla has great wind all year round, but the strongest and most consistent trade winds peak from April to September.

title.question: Are there waves for advanced riders?
title.answer: Yes, ocean-side spots like Foum El Bouir offer great wave riding conditions for surfers and wave kiters just a short drive across the peninsula.

title.question: Do I need a wetsuit?
title.answer: Yes, water temperatures in the Atlantic and lagoon call for a 3/2mm wetsuit or shorty to stay comfortable during long sessions.
